To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human gene coding for the alpha subunit of the G protein is located on chromosome 7 and encodes a polypeptide of 395 amino acid residues.

the gene for the 70,000 molecular weight subunit of the human ribosomal protein L7/L12 is located at the 5' end of the L7/L12 gene family and that the gene product is a 70,000 dalton protein that is associated with ribosomes.
the gene encoding the 50 kDa subunit of the 26S proteasome has a 3' untranslated region of 1.3 kb and that this gene has a 5' untranslated region of at least 1.3 and probably at least 1,700 kb.

the molecular genetics and biochemistry of the human insulin gene and insulin receptor.
the identification and characterization of specific gene sequences and their encoded gene products.
the development of an approach which will permit the rapid and accurate identification of specific clones.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of clone identification should be viewed as a process of elimination.
the use of a variety of different criteria, each of which is independent of others, is the only reliable way to confirm the identity of a clone.
